source.title: Comparing Kullback-Leibler Divergence and Mean Squared Error Loss in Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Taehyeon Kim; Jaehoon Oh; Nakyil Kim; Sangwook Cho; Se-Young Yun

page_placements.theme: Distillation changes noise robustness and transfers memorized information

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no document problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own noisy-label experiments on distillation objectives, but does not test fitting completely random labels or measure training error in that setting. Its results refine the claim’s noisy-label aspect only.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on memorization but reports no result of its own on fitting random labels, shuffled pixels, Gaussian-noise inputs, or training error under label noise. Figure 6 reports test accuracy under symmetric label noise; values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: Section 6 uses prior findings about memorization to motivate knowledge-distillation experiments and reports robustness through test accuracy. Figure 6 compares objectives at 40% and 80% symmetric label noise, without measuring fitting of corrupted labels. These method-performance comparisons do not establish V4's joint prediction of perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the noisy-label conclusion: KL distillation with temperature near 1 mitigates performance degradation better than extreme logit matching through infinite-temperature KL or MSE. This is a robustness conclusion, not evidence that networks fit random labels perfectly.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains student networks by knowledge distillation and varies the loss and teacher quality; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-accuracy outcome varies with the distillation objective and temperature, and with the symmetric label-noise fraction (40% versus 80%).

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100 with 40% and 80% symmetric label noise, small-temperature KL distillation gives the best reported generalization. MSE and infinite-temperature KL improve over cross-entropy below 50% noise but fail to mitigate degradation above 50%, according to Section 6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge-distillation robustness to noisy teacher-training labels depends on the distillation objective and temperature.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
record.problems: The relevant noisy-label results in Figure 6 are only shown as plots in the supplied text, with no extractable numerical values. The paper does not report student training accuracy in these experiments, so it cannot establish whether training error remains perfect.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: Figure 6 gives test-accuracy curves only as plots, without recoverable values, and does not report the training-error outcome required by V4. Cited memorization findings are prior work, not this study’s results.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time overhead for random labels and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit under increasing corruption and steady test-error degradation toward chance across the corruption range. The two noisy-label conditions report robustness of distillation objectives without training accuracy.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Whether real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels; no relevant learning trajectories are reported.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's T5 classification and V4 tested status. The statement that larger models memorize better is an interpretation of test performance, not a reported measurement of corrupted-label fitting. Figure 3 and Table 7 report training accuracy in the ordinary distillation setting, not the noisy-label experiments. Figure 6 results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment trains these networks on completely random labels and reports training error or test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The paper varies symmetric label-noise fraction and reports test accuracy, but does not report training error under noise, whether training error remains perfect, a sweep from none to all noise, or a steady test-error trend across that full range. Figure 6 values cannot be extracted numerically from the supplied text.
No experiment tests whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels or whether their removal harms true-label generalization.
No study of the order in which real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned over training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Memorization motivates the experiments; Figure 6 compares distillation objectives through test accuracy rather than testing a claim version.

tranche.reason: Section 6 uses prior memorization findings to motivate distillation robustness experiments and reports method performance, without measuring perfect fitting of corrupted labels or degradation across the full corruption range.

source_check.notes: Section 6 and Figure 6 support the statement: CIFAR-100, 40% and 80% symmetric noise, WRN-28-4 teacher and WRN-16-2 student; best generalization with KL temperature ≤1. No training-fit measurements are reported for these noisy-label experiments.
